strengths: Elegant theoretical contribution: the key insight of adjusting rewards by log(πB/πS) is clever and enables leveraging small models to approximate base model policies
Sound theoretical analysis with concrete KL divergence bounds (Theorem 1) and asymptotic guarantees (Theorem 2) with correct proofs
Practical implementation with vLLM achieving reasonable computational efficiency
Clear problem formulation and well-motivated positioning within test-time scaling literature
Systematic comparisons to relevant baselines (RSD, S-BoN variants)
weaknesses: Critical overclaiming: abstract and introduction claim GSI 'even outperforms soft best-of-n with πB', but Table 1 shows GSI achieves 51.1-51.3% vs S-BoN(big) 52.6-54.0%. On Minerva Math, GSI significantly underperforms (29.6% vs 36.4%)
Experimental results are inconsistent and modest: only ~2% improvement over S-BoN(small); RSD outperforms on OlympiadBench; improvements don't justify claims
Insufficient experimental rigor: only 2 random seeds, no confidence intervals, no significance testing, results could have substantial unreported variance

Theory-practice gap: Theorem 1 applies to reward-likelihood tilted S-BoN, but Algorithm 1 adds rejection threshold u with no theoretical justification; bounds depend on potentially large χ²(πB||πS) term with no empirical analysis
Limited scope: evaluation only on mathematical reasoning with process reward models; no assessment on alignment, safety, or generation quality tasks

Missing critical ablations: no sensitivity analysis for hyperparameters (u, β, temperature); no systematic study of when GSI works vs fails; no guidance for practitioners selecting hyperparameters on new problems
Inference efficiency claims need qualification: Table 2 shows GSI slower than RSD (0.88s vs 0.77s per step, 13.9 vs 11.6 steps), totaling ~12.2s vs ~8.9s per sample

Limited novelty: core contribution combines existing techniques (soft best-of-n, speculative decoding, rejection sampling); main novelty is log-likelihood tilt, which is elegant but somewhat incremental
Weak experimental presentation: Figure 2 lacks hyperparameter sensitivity analysis; limited discussion of why performance degrades on certain datasets

strengths: Clear theoretical contribution with Theorem 1 providing formal KL divergence guarantees on approximating the optimal tilted policy, grounding the approach mathematically
Elegant core insight: tilting rewards by log-likelihood ratio log(π_B/π_S) is intuitive and theoretically motivated, elegantly accounting for model differences
Consistent empirical improvements over RSD and S-BoN(π_S) across all three mathematical reasoning benchmarks (51.1-51.3% vs 48.5-48.8% mean accuracy)
Practical efficiency: achieves 0.88-2.05s per step with GSI vs 1.14-2.76s for S-BoN(π_B), enabling real speedups on reasoning tasks
Well-organized presentation with clear algorithm specification, transparent experimental setup, and available code
weaknesses: Significant theory-practice gap: Theorem 1 covers π^{r,n}_{β,S} but Algorithm 1 adds unjustified rejection sampling step (lines 7-14) not covered by theory; Theorem 2 is much weaker, only showing convergence as n→∞
Theoretical bounds appear impractical: required n scales exponentially in β∥r∥_∞ (factor e^40 with given hyperparameters), suggesting bounds are loose and may lack practical utility
Insufficient experimental rigor: only 2 random seeds without error bars or significance tests, making it unclear if improvements are meaningful; differences often 1-3% within noise margins

Overstated claims about outperforming S-BoN(big): paper claims GSI 'surpasses' big model in some cases, but OlympiadBench shows S-BoN(big) achieving 42.5% vs GSI 41.2% at n=64, and Minerva Math shows 29.6% vs 36.4%
Strong coverage assumption (Eq. 3) treated superficially: critical for all guarantees but requires π_B support ⊆ π_S support; deserves deeper discussion of practical validity and failure modes
No hyperparameter sensitivity analysis: β and threshold u identified as empirically selected with no ablation studies, sensitivity analysis, or principled selection guidance provided
Limited experimental scope: only mathematical reasoning with Qwen models; generality to other domains (alignment, safety) and model sizes/architectures unvalidated
Incomplete scaling analysis: Figure 2 stops at n=256 despite acknowledged need to investigate beyond, limiting understanding of convergence behavior
Missing comparisons: no evaluation against other recent test-time scaling methods beyond RSD, limiting positioning in the literature

strengths: Novel theoretical contribution with KL divergence bounds on distributional fidelity (Theorem 1), which is stronger than prior work like RSD
Elegant and well-motivated technical insight: reward tilting via r̃ = r + (1/β)log(πB/πS) is intuitive and principled
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 5 benchmarks with proper statistical reporting (95% CI over 3 seeds) and detailed ablations
Consistent empirical improvements over RSD and soft best-of-n with draft model across all datasets
Clear presentation with well-designed figures, algorithm descriptions, and reasoning traces providing qualitative insights
Convergence guarantee on expected reward at rate O(1/√n) (Theorem 2)
weaknesses: Limited component novelty: combines existing techniques (speculative decoding, soft best-of-n) with a relatively simple modification; theoretical analysis largely follows Verdun et al.

Theoretical guarantees have significant limitations: coverage assumption may be violated, sample complexity scales with χ²(πB||πS) + e^(2β||r||∞) which can be very large, Assumption 2 is strong and not obviously satisfied
Rejection sampling step (Algorithm 1, lines 6-11) lacks theoretical justification despite being crucial for empirical performance
Modest practical improvements over RSD: 1-2% accuracy gains on average, with lower acceptance rates (76.7% vs 94.9%) and slower inference time per step (0.43s vs 0.34s)
Hyperparameter tuning challenges: threshold u is problem-dependent and n-dependent (Pareto frontier in Figure 9), no adaptive scheme proposed despite clear evidence
Incomplete comparison to SPECS due to unavailable code and different evaluation protocols (N=500 vs N=100)
Limited experimental scope: only math reasoning and STEM tasks with single model family (Qwen2.5-Math), no evaluation on general domains or robustness to PRM quality
Computational overhead not fully characterized; wall-clock times reported as unreliable; multiple forward passes needed for log-likelihood computation

strengths: Meaningful theoretical contribution: Theorem 1 provides KL divergence bounds to optimal tilted distribution, stronger than RSD's reward-only guarantees
Elegant reward tilting approach (r̃ = r + (1/β)log(πB/πS)) with solid mathematical motivation and intuitive interpretation
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 5 benchmarks, 2 model families (1B-14B parameters), 3 random seeds with 95% confidence intervals
Consistent empirical improvements over RSD across all settings; up to 28% latency reduction vs S-BoN with base model
Reproducibility: detailed implementation details, promised code release, full hyperparameter documentation, hardware specifications
Sound technical execution with rigorous proofs and proper statistical methodology
weaknesses: Limited novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (speculative decoding, soft best-of-n, reward alignment) with incremental log-likelihood tilt

Theoretical bound tightness issues: Theorem 1 bound depends on χ²(πB||πS) which is large in practice (1.48-3.91 in experiments); authors acknowledge bound is not necessarily tight and provide no empirical validation of KL distance
Strong coverage assumption (Assumption 1) with limited discussion of robustness; Assumption 2 for Theorem 2 may not hold generally
Experimental scope limited to step-by-step reasoning tasks with single PRM; no evaluation on one-shot generation despite theoretical applicability; sensitivity to PRM quality/size unknown

Efficiency claims need nuance: GSI has lower acceptance rates (70-90% vs RSD's 90-100%), is slower than RSD in absolute terms (Table 1), and 28% improvement is relative to S-BoN base; PRM overhead (~40% of runtime) significantly limits end-to-end speedup
Hyperparameter sensitivity: β=20 and u=0.5 chosen empirically; Figure 11 indicates adaptive threshold schedule would improve performance but not implemented; no principled guidance provided
Lower acceptance rates of GSI vs RSD not thoroughly discussed; no analysis of why correct reasoning steps are sometimes rejected (Example 2, Figure 3)
Missing ablations: no evaluation of PRM size/quality sensitivity, alternative tilting schemes, or analysis of χ² dependence

No direct experimental comparison to concurrent SPECS work (only comparison to paper results with different evaluation protocols: 500 vs 100 samples); SPECS outperforms GSI on OlympiadBench at small n
Presentation: coverage assumption could be better motivated; claim of 'first speculative method with distributional guarantees' overstated given concurrent SPECS work; Figure 1 text too small
